title: Juniper and the Harbor
premise: In the port town of Grayharbor, 1792, Cyrus Underhill has spent twelve years as her father's apprentice in a type foundry, invisible behind the shop's silence and the name she was given to hide her sex. When revolutionary soldiers requisition the town, they seize the foundry's master ledger — a record of every printer, smuggler, and dissident who ever bought type from Underhill & Sons. Cyrus discovers her father cut a hidden second ledger into spare type blocks, and she alone can read its coded impressions. Over one winter she must carry the evidence past three army checkpoints to a ship called Juniper before the century turns, trading pieces of her own history for each passage. She reaches the harbor on New Year's Eve, burns the false records that would have condemned forty families, and chooses at last to sign her own name.
about_author: Silas Villalobos is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal mill towns. He writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'and others.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Letters
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She cuts type by lamplight while her father sleeps, establishing the foundry, her hidden identity as 'Cyrus,' and the town's uneasy quiet. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Grayharbor in Fog
chapters.summary: Cyrus walks the docks delivering proofs, mapping the town's factions: loyalist merchants, harbor smugglers, the print circle. POV shifts briefly to harbormaster's daughter Tamsin. Beat: belonging observed from outside.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers in gray coats post notices; the army claims the town and demands all business ledgers within ten days. Cyrus watches her father hide nothing — he has no second ledger, or so she believes. Beat: dread arriving politely.

chapters.title: What Father Kept
chapters.summary: Sorting type cases at night, Cyrus finds blocks whose reversed impressions form coded names — a secret ledger cut into metal over twelve years, including entries she never knew existed. Beat: betrayal braided with awe.

chapters.title: The Inventory Men
chapters.summary: Army clerk Aldous Vane inventories the shop with unsettling courtesy, asking questions about customers long gone. Cyrus lies fluently for the first time. Beat: fear discovering it has a talent.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how young Juniper became 'Cyrus' after her mother's death, and why her father taught her that names are dangerous currency. Beat: grief explained as inheritance.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Cyrus carries the first four type blocks sewn into her coat toward the river bridge checkpoint, learning the soldiers' rhythms. A near-search is deflected by Tamsin's intervention. Beat: terror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Juniper at Anchor
chapters.summary: She meets Captain Osei of the smuggling brig Juniper, who agrees to carry 'cargo' but not yet people or causes. Beat: cautious alliance, price named.

chapters.title: Names in Metal
chapters.summary: Deciphering more blocks at night, Cyrus recognizes her own mother's name among the coded entries — her father recorded the family too. Beat: the ledger becomes personal.

chapters.title: Vane Returns
chapters.summary: Aldous Vane reappears off-duty, buying a keepsake type block, probing whether the Underhills kept 'working copies.' His politeness curdles. Beat: the hunter learns patience.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin reveals her father logs every departing vessel for the army; she offers falsified manifests in exchange for Cyrus erasing her brother's name from any list. Beat: complicity shared.

chapters.title: The Print Circle Scattered
chapters.summary: Two printers are arrested; their shop burned. Cyrus watches neighbors look away, understanding the silences she inherited are now everyone's survival. Beat: communal cowardice, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Cyrus moves the second cache through the tollhouse road disguised as a delivery girl for a cooper. A soldier recognizes her hands as a cutter's. Beat: identity nearly costing everything.

chapters.title: Father's Confession
chapters.summary: Her father admits he cut the ledger not for rebellion but insurance — leverage against the day someone came collecting debts. He never meant her to carry it. Beat: love expressed as failure.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Osei names his fee: passage plus the Juniper's debt cleared requires Cyrus to forge army shipping papers — real forgery, real gallows risk. Beat: survival quantified.

chapters.title: Learning to Lie in Lead
chapters.summary: Cyrus cuts counterfeit seals and signatures at night, discovering she is better at deception than her father ever was. Beat: dark self-recognition.

chapters.title: Winter Quarters
chapters.summary: Soldiers billet in the foundry itself; Cyrus hides blocks inside hollowed type cases under their noses. A young soldier, Emmerich, shows unexpected decency. Beat: enemy humanized.

chapters.title: The Brother's Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's brother appears alive in a coded entry — listed as an informant. Cyrus must decide whether to tell her. Beat: truth as a weapon against an ally.

chapters.title: Telling Tamsin
chapters.summary: Cyrus tells the truth; Tamsin shatters, then chooses to keep helping anyway, separating her brother from his crimes. Beat: forgiveness as labor, not feeling.

chapters.title: Emmerich's Question
chapters.summary: The young soldier catches Cyrus mid-deception but asks instead what the war is for. She gives him an answer that costs her nothing and changes him. Beat: mercy in wartime.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Gate
chapters.summary: The harbor gate checkpoint tightens after an escape attempt; passes now require countersigns Cyrus cannot forge. The plan stalls. Beat: walls closing.

chapters.title: Vane Closes In
chapters.summary: Vane presents her father with recovered fragments of coded type from the burned print shop. Her father takes the blame entirely and is arrested. Beat: sacrifice as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Alone in the requisitioned foundry, Cyrus confronts twelve years of learned silence and decides silence ends with her. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Osei
chapters.summary: Cyrus offers Osei the full ledger — leverage worth a fortune — if he sails on New Year's Eve and takes her father's case of evidence. He warns her what armies do to harbors. Beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Pass
chapters.summary: Using everything she's learned, Cyrus cuts a flawless gate pass — signing it with a dead man's name, then, impulsively, adding her own initial where no one will look. Beat: identity reclaimed in miniature.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Cyrus is summoned to account for discrepancies in the foundry inventory. She performs innocence so well she frightens herself. Beat: the mask fitting too well.

chapters.title: Father in the Cells
chapters.summary: Visiting her father through bars, she learns the last cipher key he never taught her — hidden in the lesson of her own name. Beat: inheritance completed.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Manifest
chapters.summary: Tamsin falsifies the Juniper's departure papers for New Year's Eve, knowing discovery means transportation. Beat: friendship proven at cost.

chapters.title: The Storm Delay
chapters.summary: A gale traps the fleet in port; the century will turn with the evidence still ashore. Cyrus must hold everything together three more days. Beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Emmerich's Choice
chapters.summary: Emmerich discovers the hidden cache during a routine search — and reports the room clean. He asks only to be posted elsewhere. Beat: complicity passed like a candle.

chapters.title: Vane's Trap
chapters.summary: Vane announces a full search of all departures on New Year's Eve, having deduced a ship will sail. He suspects the foundry but lacks proof. Beat: the net drawn tight.

chapters.title: Dividing the Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus splits the evidence: half to the Juniper via Tamsin's crates, half sewn into her own coat. If either fails, the other survives. Beat: strategy as devotion.

chapters.title: New Year's Eve: The Harbor
chapters.summary: Snow, lanterns, crowds celebrating the century's turn — cover for movement. Cyrus reaches the quay as the Juniper makes ready. Beat: breathless momentum.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three Again
chapters.summary: At the gate, Vane himself inspects papers. He reads her forged pass, looks at her face, and hesitates — recognizing craft, perhaps kinship. Beat: climax of nerve.

chapters.title: The Cutter's Mark
chapters.summary: Vane lets her pass — then follows. On the quay he confronts her; she offers him the one thing he wants: acknowledgment that he sees clearly in a blind time. He turns away. Beat: antagonist granted dignity.

chapters.title: Sailing
chapters.summary: The Juniper clears the harbor with the evidence aboard as midnight bells ring. Cyrus watches from the crowd, anonymous, carrying her half still. Beat: triumph shadowed by unfinished work.

chapters.title: After the Century Turns
chapters.summary: January: the army withdraws as political winds shift; prisoners are released in the general amnesty. Her father comes home diminished. Beat: survival without vindication.

chapters.title: The Foundry Reopened
chapters.summary: Father and daughter reopen the shop. He offers to restore her legal name; she declines — Cyrus is hers now, chosen rather than assigned. Beat: reconciliation on new terms.

chapters.title: What the Ship Carried
chapters.summary: Word returns that the Juniper delivered the ledger to printers abroad; the names were published, the informants exposed, the forty families safe. Tamsin's brother flees the country. Beat: consequence distributed fairly.

chapters.title: Juniper and the Harbor
chapters.summary: Cyrus cuts a new typeface of her own design and prints the first broadside signed plainly: set by Cyrus Underhill. The harbor fog lifts. Beat: belonging achieved — she belongs to her own name.
